reviewed_in: issue #672: every npm and cargo acknowledgement re-reviewed against the 2026-10-20 lockfiles before the 2026-10-31 expiry; eleven npm findings remediated by targeted dev-dependency updates, the rest re-argued with fresh paths. Prior review: issue #35 (2026-08-11).
how_this_file_is_used: scripts/supply-chain-gate.mjs re-runs both audits against the current lockfiles on every verification run. A cargo finding whose package is absent from `cargo tree --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --edges normal,build` is classified mechanically and needs no entry here. Everything else must be listed below with a reachability argument and a review date. An unlisted finding fails the gate; a listed finding whose review_by has passed fails the gate. Acknowledgements expire on purpose - the alternative is a permanent excuse.

npm.shipped_artifact: The Compy installer contains the Rust executable and the Vite build output (tauri.conf.json build.frontendDist = ../dist). bundle.resources and bundle.externalBin are unset, so no node_modules content is packaged; only code the Vite build actually imports reaches dist/. Every devDependency advisory below is therefore a build-integrity or developer-workstation concern, which is a reachability statement, not a dismissal: a compromised build tool would reach the installer through dist/. The one production-dependency entry (fflate) carries its own evidence that its code is absent from dist/.

braces.why: braces GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm: stack exhaustion when expanding a deeply nested brace pattern. This is the vulnerable package itself. The only path is the shadcn devDependency, a component-scaffolding CLI that nothing in package.json scripts, the Vite build or the test suite runs; the shadcn MCP server in .mcp.json launches its own pinned shadcn@4.19.0 through npx, not this copy. Its fast-glob calls take shadcn's own literal patterns (tsconfig.*, tailwind.config.*, **/package.json, **/*.css), and it uses ts-morph through in-memory or compilerOptions-only Projects, so no deeply nested pattern from any input reaches braces. No patched braces release exists (3.0.3 is the newest), and every shadcn release from 2.0.0 through 4.22.1 still pins ts-morph ^26 and fast-glob ^3.3.3; npm's offered fix is a downgrade to shadcn@1.0.0, which is an owner decision recorded in #672, not a lockfile change.

fflate.why: GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98: unzipSync can loop forever on a malformed ZIP64 archive. This is the one production-dependency finding: fflate 0.6.10 is nested under three-stdlib, which @react-three/drei depends on; the top-level fflate 0.8.3 is outside the vulnerable range. three-stdlib uses fflate only in its file loaders and exporters. src/ imports only Edges, Html, Grid, OrbitControls and shaderMaterial from drei and never imports three-stdlib or fflate, and the 2026-10-20 production build tree-shakes fflate out: three error strings present in fflate 0.6.10's own ESM build (invalid block type, invalid length/literal, unexpected EOF) occur nowhere in dist/. Compy also loads no ZIP, KMZ, 3MF, FBX or USDZ file at all. The patched fflate 0.6.11 is inside three-stdlib's declared ^0.6.9 range, but bumping a production dependency was outside #672's dev-only scope, so it is recommended there for a separate owner-approved change; the earlier review date reflects that a fix is available.

cargo.note: Compy's own Rust source references none of these crates: a case-sensitive search for quick_xml, crossbeam, rayon, anyhow and downcast_mut across the 55 .rs files under src-tauri/ and src-tauri/Cargo.toml returns nothing (re-run 2026-10-20). They arrive transitively: through Tauri and its plugins, through sysinfo (crossbeam-epoch) and through adlx (anyhow). Paths below are from `cargo tree --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -e normal -i <crate>` against the 2026-10-20 Cargo.lock. The rustls and rustls-webpki findings (RUSTSEC-2026-0285, -0346, -0348, -0349 and -0382) were never acknowledged, because the updater reaches them on live TLS traffic. A semver-compatible Cargo.lock update (issue #675) fixed them instead: rustls 0.23.42 -> 0.23.46 and rustls-webpki 0.103.13 -> 0.103.16. The same update moved crossbeam-epoch 0.9.18 -> 0.9.21 and anyhow 1.0.102 -> 1.0.104, so the RUSTSEC-2026-0204 and RUSTSEC-2026-0190 acknowledgements were removed.

RUSTSEC-2026-0194.why: Quadratic run time in the duplicate-attribute check of BytesStart::attributes(), a denial of service that needs attacker-controlled XML to be parsed. Neither copy in the Windows build parses anything. 0.37.5 is used by tauri-winrt-notification 0.7.2 only through quick_xml::escape::escape, to escape text into toast XML it writes itself; it never constructs a Reader or NsReader. 0.39.4 arrives only through plist 1.9.0 in tauri-utils 2.9.2, whose sole plist use (config.rs file_associations_plist) builds a Dictionary from config, parses nothing and has no caller in tauri, tauri-build, tauri-codegen or tauri-runtime-wry; tauri's one plist parse (process.rs plist::from_file) is compiled only for macOS. Patched at >=0.41.0, a semver-major step that only tauri-winrt-notification and plist can take.
paths: quick-xml@0.39.4 <- plist@1.9.0 <- tauri-utils@2.9.2 <- tauri@2.11.2 (runtime) and tauri-build@2.6.2 (build)

RUSTSEC-2026-0195.why: Unbounded namespace-declaration allocation in NsReader, a memory-exhaustion denial of service that needs attacker-controlled XML to be read through NsReader. Same two copies and the same evidence as RUSTSEC-2026-0194: 0.37.5 is only ever used to escape text that tauri-winrt-notification writes, and the plist path that carries 0.39.4 parses nothing on Windows, so no NsReader is constructed anywhere in the shipped build. Patched at >=0.41.0, a Tauri-side upgrade.
paths: quick-xml@0.39.4 <- plist@1.9.0 <- tauri-utils@2.9.2 <- tauri@2.11.2 (runtime) and tauri-build@2.6.2 (build)

RUSTSEC-2026-0368.why: ZipArchive::extract creates symlinks whose attacker-chosen targets escape the destination (verified on macOS and Linux). zip 4.6.1 is linked only by tauri-plugin-updater 2.10.1, which on Windows reaches extract_zip from install_inner only for an archive whose bytes already passed verify_signature (minisign, against the pubkey in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json plugins.updater) inside download(); the install IPC command accepts only the bytes resource that download produced, and Compy never calls the plugin's Rust Update::install. Compy's own updater artifacts are not zips at all (bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts is true, not "v1Compatible"), so a malicious archive would need a signature from Compy's private release key. No fix is reachable: the newest updater (2.14.0, and 3.0.0-alpha.3) still requires zip ^4, and 4.6.1 is the newest 4.x; patched at >=9.0.0.

RUSTSEC-2026-0369.why: extract() applies Unix permissions through extracted symlinks without confining the target. Unix permission bits have no effect on the Windows-only shipped build, and the only extraction (tauri-plugin-updater 2.10.1 extract_zip) runs on bytes that already passed minisign verification against Compy's updater pubkey; Compy publishes no zipped updater artifacts. Same reachability and the same absent fix as RUSTSEC-2026-0368.

RUSTSEC-2026-0367.why: SUID, SGID and sticky bits from an archive's external attributes survive extraction. Those bits do not exist on Windows, the only target Compy ships, and the only extraction (tauri-plugin-updater 2.10.1 extract_zip) runs on bytes that already passed minisign verification against Compy's updater pubkey; Compy publishes no zipped updater artifacts. Same reachability and the same absent fix as RUSTSEC-2026-0368.

RUSTSEC-2025-0081.why: Unmaintained, with no advisory of a defect and no maintained 0.9 successor. unic-char-property is in the runtime graph through unic-ucd-ident 0.9.0 and urlpattern 0.3.0, an unconditional tauri-utils 2.9.2 dependency that Tauri uses only to parse and match the "remote" URL patterns of a capability (tauri-utils acl RemoteUrlPattern, matched in tauri ipc/authority.rs). Compy's four capability files under src-tauri/capabilities/ declare no "remote" block, so no pattern is ever parsed from Compy's configuration and no web content can feed one. Retiring it is a Tauri-side change; tracked so the warning cannot quietly turn into a vulnerability without a re-review.

RUSTSEC-2026-0386.why: RUSTSEC-2026-0386: AsyncFd::new and its sibling constructors accept a file descriptor without taking ownership, which violates I/O safety. AsyncFd exists only on Unix: tokio 1.52.3 declares src/io/async_fd.rs and tokio::io::unix inside cfg_net_unix!, which expands to #[cfg(all(unix, feature = "net"))], so none of the unsound code is compiled for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Compy's own Rust source does not depend on or name tokio (a search for tokio, AsyncFd, RawFd and OwnedFd under src-tauri/src and src-tauri/Cargo.toml returns nothing, re-run 2026-10-23). It arrives only transitively, through tauri, reqwest/hyper and tauri-plugin-updater. The fix (tokio 1.52.3 -> 1.54.1, offered by `cargo update -p tokio`) is a minor-version change to the async runtime of the shipped app. That is outside #672's scope, which keeps src-tauri/ read-only, so it is left for its own slice with cargo test and the Windows gates.
